summary: The revision fits a solo bootstrapped founder better: a 3-month build with public research first, disposable test setups, no custom compiler, realistic capacity and a partner channel. Credibility is still the gate. An unknown founder with Windows, CTF and CompTIA credentials must win CTOs and partners against named researchers. First revenue lands around month 4-6, and the founder's detection skills stay unused.

objections.objection: Credibility is still unproven and everything depends on it. The plan now puts 2-3 write-ups before selling, but the direct and partner channels both need the founder to look like a coding-agent security expert. Established boutiques already publish deep coding-agent work, such as Christian Schneider's ten-domain assessment and cheat sheet. Pentest and vCISO firms will not resell an unknown solo tester's red team until they see a finding or a reference client.

Time to first revenue is long for a founder with no capital. The plan needs 3 months to build the test environment, the 30+ case suite and the write-ups, plus about a month to learn agent managed settings, sandbox and hook semantics, GitHub Actions attack paths and SOC 2 control wording. With the 2-week test after that and a typical first-deal cycle, the first $6,500 arrives around month 4-6. The founder has plenty of time, so this is survivable but not fast. A paid one-repository CI test could close earlier.

There is still an upfront cost and hurdle before the first sprint. E&O and cyber insurance, rules of engagement, an authorisation letter, a liability cap and a DPA are all needed. A new solo firm with no claims history may struggle to get cover, and premiums are paid before any income. Disposable-environment testing removes most of the operational liability.

The founder's strongest asset, Windows detection engineering, is still unused, so the business rests on newly learned skills. A detection add-on is only an open question. Endpoint-managed Claude Code settings reach Windows through the registry, so a Windows/MDM-hardening angle exists, but the concept does not use it.

One person carries both selling and keeping up with four agents' changing settings. Dropping the policy compiler helps, but the private injection suite and coverage matrix still need re-validation with every agent release, on top of delivery and sales at about 2 sprints a month.

strongest_point: A fixed-fee service with near-zero running costs and a disposable-environment red team built on the founder's offensive and Python skills. Partner resale suits someone without a sales team.
what_would_change_my_mind: Within 3 months, 2-3 public reproducible coding-agent or CI-agent injection write-ups, at least one acknowledged by a vendor or maintainer, plus a talk accepted at a BSides or similar event.
2 of 10 interviewed pentest, SOC 2 readiness or vCISO firms sign a written referral or resale agreement, and 1 paid deposit or one-repository CI test closes by month 4.
An insurance quote for E&O and cyber cover under about $3k a year for a new solo firm.

Fit would improve with a Windows-fleet variant: MDM- or registry-delivered managed settings plus Sysmon or EDR rules for agent-spawned shells and MCP processes, sold through MSPs that manage Windows developer fleets.

resolved_prior.objection: Credibility gap with the named buyer, with no time planned before the sales test.
resolved_prior.note: Partly addressed. Write-ups before selling and 3 months of build time are now planned, but the credibility itself is still unproven and is the main dependency.

resolved_prior.objection: Core strengths unused and three new domains to learn; a 1-month MVP is unrealistic.
resolved_prior.note: The timeline is fixed (3 months), but the Windows detection strengths are still unused and the learning load is unchanged.

resolved_prior.objection: First-customer plan exceeds a solo founder's reach.
resolved_prior.note: The success signal is reset to partner commitments and one deposit, with first revenue expected around month 3-5. That is realistic, though the partners still need credibility.

resolved_prior.objection: Liability risk of red-teaming production credentials, plus insurance cost.
resolved_prior.note: Testing now runs in a disposable fork with scoped tokens by default, plus paperwork and insurance. The remaining insurance cost and the risk of being refused cover are minor.

resolved_prior.objection: The income model overstated one person's capacity.
resolved_prior.note: The rationale now assumes 2 sprints a month, about $13k gross.

resolved_prior.objection: Vendor managed policies shrink the setup work and force constant re-learning.
resolved_prior.note: The core is moved to red teams and re-tests and the compiler is dropped, which reduces upkeep. Keeping up with the platforms is still a solo burden.
